speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is causing this, can you tell me if you are passing stool or having gas, and have you noticed any vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The combination of abdominal distension, feeding difficulties, irritability (fussiness), and specifically pain that worsens with abdominal palpation is highly suggestive of intussusception in an 8-month-old infant. This is a surgical emergency requiring immediate evaluation.
